t: You're looking at the statue of Alfred the Great in Trinity Church Square, Southwark, thought to be London's oldest outdoor statue. It's really two statues in one. The lower portion comes from a Roman statue of the late first or early second century AD, while the top is a Coade stone addition in medieval style, made in the late eighteenth or early nineteenth century. It depicts Alfred, who was King of the West Saxons and then of the Anglo-Saxons, and whose reforms to administration and the military prompted lasting change in England.
